Hashtags and Uprising in Bangladesh, July 2024

This study presents observations based on 410 TikTok videos and 1,031 Facebook posts about the Bangladesh quota reform movement, from 7 July to 5 August 2024. Read the background, see which divisions the posts point to, explore posts and engagement by date, or see how the hashtags connect.

About the data

The posts were collected by searching protest hashtags, so the counts describe this sample and not all activity on either platform. A post found under several hashtags is counted once, and posts unrelated to Bangladesh were removed. Engagement figures are totals at the time of collection, assigned to the day the post was published; all dates and times are in UTC. TikTok saves and Facebook likes and views exist for one platform only and are shown separately, with views recorded for about 82% of Facebook posts.

The protest background and most event notes come from the Al Jazeera report cited below. The notes for 14 July, 16 July, 31 July and 3 August are additional background, and none of them are derived from the dataset.

Background source: Chughtai, A., & Ali, M. (2024, August 7). How Bangladesh's 'Gen Z' protests brought down PM Sheikh Hasina. Al Jazeera.

Where the posts point

How to read this map

The map counts a post under a division when its caption names one of that division's districts in English or Bengali, or one of a few Dhaka neighbourhoods and university tags; a post can count under several divisions, and most posts name no place. Division outlines are dissolved from upazila boundaries by geoBoundaries (CC BY 4.0; Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics / OCHA), via the bd-geojson package, and are approximate. The map shows which places posts talk about, not where they were posted from.

Qualitative assessment

Method

This study looks back at protest content that activists shared publicly on Facebook and TikTok, using a non-participant, observational approach informed by digital ethnography (Tarafdar & Ray, 2021). Hashtags were the baseline for collection because they gather shared voices and topical communities. Using the 42 most relevant hashtags identified by Subat and Fichman (2025), we collected posts dated from 7 July 2024 through repeated searches between 1 and 20 October 2025. The corpus held 11,311 Facebook posts with 268,817 comments and 418 TikTok posts with 384,548 comments. After cleaning, we selected the two most engaged posts per day by stratified purposive sampling. The assessment covers a sample of 120 posts and 6,000 comments from 7 July to 5 August 2024.

Summary of findings

Two researchers coded every post and comment in the sample; the comments were chosen at random under each post.

Statistics

Choose counts or percentages, show or hide columns, filter categories, and click a column heading to sort.

Intra-actions in posts

60 coded posts per platform.

Intercoder agreement 81.1% (Cohen's kappa 0.811); chi-square 11.827, 5 degrees of freedom, p = 0.049.

Interactions in comments

3,000 coded comments per platform.

Intercoder agreement 84.2%; chi-square 1,543.45, p = 0.01.

Codebook

The codebook sorts digital protest output into two groups. Intra-actions describe what a post does for the movement and have five codes: solidarity, recruitment, coordination, propagation and conflict. Interactions describe how people respond in the comments and have thirteen codes, from hostile forms such as provocation, mocking and name calling, through sarcasm, satire and irony, to supportive forms such as encouragement, calls for justice, emotional appeal and cultural reference. Each code is counted as the number of posts or comments that fit it.
